Title: Fullstack Java Developer
Likes: The salary is decent, but there's a lot of benefits that you could count as bonus. There's also an abundance of certification courses, programmes and events to expand your knowledge within your field, and soft skills as a consultant. Capgemini is all about learning. If you're not satisfied with the customer, you likely have a chanceto either switch teams or project. As an employee, you get a lot of freedom to do your work. This goes hand-in-hand with the new memo that everybody is their own leader. Job security is also excellent, in that Capgemini has a lot of tolerance for employees who fall behind. I've never seen anyone get fired - rather they always want to hire more people. If you complete a certification or a course, you get appraisal in your office; colleagues and leaders will congratulate you....Read More
Dislikes: I agree with most other review that the biggest problem is middle-managment. That is, a lot of managers act unprofessional, pushy and sometimes abusive. They also like to play favorites. Capgemini doesn't really do anything with this issue, because I think they're kind of dependent on them to manage all the thousands of offices and departments. For example, I wanted to se certain career goals through the "MyPath" programme. But instead of respecting my goals, my manager added more goals I never wanted and weighted them differently than what I did. So they should really rename it to "TheirPath". I've also experienced managers treat me unfairly compared to other team members (probably because they didn't like me), a manager bragging about the money they made from recruitment, aggressive/snappy behavior and lots more. They also never respect work-life boundaries. It doesn't matter if you do an outstanding job for the customer, if you don't do what they ask you to do outside work hours you might as well quit the job. If you just have normal 9-5 days they will throw things at you like taking a certification, host events, move tables/chairs etc. all outside work hours - even though none of this is mentioned in the contract (yes, I did contact a lawyer to double check that). I also agree that there's a lot of micromanagment, they always try to correct everything about you that they don't like. A sort of narcissistic "I can change him/her" attitude. The office cultures I've seen is also kind of bad, there's always competition between employees even during lunch breaks. Toxic comments and bad treatment towards each other instead of building each other up, and almost nobody practice the seven core Capgemini values....Read More

First let me start by the biggest thing positive about this organization. I joined when times were turbulent, Clients were firing contractors due to Corona from left or right. In came Mr. Aiman Ezzat with a announcement saying none of the recent hires or existing employees would be asked to let go. I stayed without any assignments for 7 months, got confirmed and eventually in the month of December I finally found my first assignment, had this been any other employer, I would have been anxious in the last bone of my body.

And from what I know I am not alone, there are 19 more candidates from all over India who got selected only for NL, Sweden I don't even know how many.
Now to be said this is overkill, let me give you more, I spent countless hours taking interview for I&D India, for which I was given extra allowance. Since the onset of Corona I didn't went to Capgemini office a single day except for completing my India Transfer formalities. I was able to see my newly-born daughter grow in front of my eyes, without loosing respect with my peers, both in Capgemini and Client, got an onsite opportunity and promotion with hike at the same time. Company has good policies over all, you get 24 leaves in a year each month 2 leaves are credited in your account. Salary Hike- Even with best rating, a person is lucky to receive double digits hike. Otherwise usual hike is 0-5%. They would keep on acquiring companies and put it as expense on company balance sheet and even give 0 hike to employee.
Variable Pay- They wont pay for the last/resigning year and at least 6months variable is lost.
Shift Allowance- I worked in a lot of projects, not even a single PM informed about this. They would ask to work in shifts but won't pay shift allowance mostly.
HR policies- HR is the weakest in CG. In case of any conflict they would ask to connect to the manager/supervisor and refrain to interfere.
Training- Only given as per project requirement. Every employee has to mandatory do 40+hrs/year. Earlier they were providing project code for training but it is stopped.
Travel- Worst, Eg if a person is travelling for a meeting for 2 days then the PM can approve the stay for only 1 day i.e. there is no last day stay. So this  person has to leave hotel on last day, report office for meeting and directly leave from office to base location.
Cost Cutting- Project management will hide policies in the name of cost cutting.
Onsite- Is very minimal and the management is always ready to travel themselves in case something comes up.
Project Work- Not much exciting and mostly you would be working on multiple projects 2 or 3 to optimize your work and cost savings.
New Joiners- Have a bond for 2 years and they have stopped default promotions which were there earlier for fresher's.
Career Growth- Very minimal, unless someone leaves there are hardly any promotions. Only the fresher's not laterals have good chance....Read More
